why: Quote and identifier both check out; the CONSEQUENCE attached to the quoted field is false by measurement. (1) Quote verbatim at plugins/manifest-reference.md#lspservers (was line 262 of the retired plugins-reference page), whole line read, no reversing second half; the only adjacent qualifier is :266 ('restartOnCrash and shutdownTimeout require Claude Code v2.1.205 or later'), which does not reverse it. (2) Cited claude.ts:2075 sits inside the doc-comment (2053-2090) for CLAUDE_UNREAD_LSP_FIELDS at :2081; the eight names match exactly, the warning plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread is emitted at :2158-2164, and the capability built at :2166-2177 carries only command/args/languages/env/workspaceFolder. So the declared-but-unread half is CONFIRMED. (3) The claim's harm for restartOnCrash is inverted. Nessy has no LSP restart mechanism at all: LspService.fail() (pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:382-387) is terminal, the read loop throws 'lsp-process-closed' on process exit (:282), and nothing respawns; SessionManager provisions LspService once per agent construction (getOrCreateAgentUnchecked, :11597-11660) and shouldRetainPiLspService only disposes a non-ready service at the NEXT agent construction. The repo's own deviation audit already states it: 'a crashed server stays failed forever' (2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:153). So an author who sets restartOnCrash:false gets exactly the documented outcome (crashed server left stopped), and there is no crash-loop for the flag to stop. 'gets neither' is refuted for the very field the quoted sentence is about; the divergence on that field runs the other way (the documented default true is what we do not implement). Secondary: the whole plugin-LSP surface is Pi-only (provider === 'pi' at :11597 and :12313), a harness this fork built itself, so Claude's supervisor semantics were never being mirrored. Not one of the nine inert-worklist section 3 owner decisions, but it is a recorded scope decision - docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-instruction-memory-and-diagnostics.md 'Deliberately out of scope': 'restartOnCrash / maxRestarts. Absent repo-wide; LSP crash handling is terminal by design today ... Restart policy is its own decision' and 'A per-server diagnostics flag. Nothing parses one' - and it is tracked open as parity-audit row P8. The channel choice (warning diagnostic, not a deferred row) is itself a measured decision recorded at claude.ts:2053-2080 and plan 2026-07-31-plugins-and-marketplace.md C5.
correctedState: All eight fields (transport, initializationOptions, settings, startupTimeout, shutdownTimeout, restartOnCrash, maxRestarts, diagnostics) are indeed parsed-but-unread at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2081, with a named plugin.format.claude_lsp_fields_unread warning at :2158 and a capability carrying only command/args/languages/env/workspaceFolder at :2166. But the user-visible harm is not what was claimed. restartOnCrash: Nessy never restarts a crashed language server (LspService.fail() at pi-harness/lsp-service.ts:382-387 is terminal; no respawn anywhere), so restartOnCrash:false is satisfied by accident and no crash-loop is possible; the unimplemented behaviour is the documented DEFAULT true. diagnostics: this half stands - automatic post-edit diagnostic injection is real and on by default (AGENT_FLAGS.editFeedbackEnabled true at SessionManager.ts:454, recordPiLspDiagnostics at :2351 folded into the edit-feedback payload via buildEditFeedbackRunner at :5286), so diagnostics:false is genuinely not honoured. The concrete harm the claim missed is startupTimeout: LspService defaults to 12s (lsp-service.ts:142) while the only two official catalogue plugins that declare the field (jdtls-lsp, kotlin-lsp) ask for 120s, so they abort at initialize today - recorded as OWED in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-plugins-and-marketplace.md row C5. The whole plugin-LSP path is Pi-only (provider === 'pi'), which is a separate already-recorded audit row (P8).
